name: Suitcase Deadlift
description: The suitcase deadlift is a unilateral variation where a single weight (barbell, dumbbell, or kettlebell) is lifted from the floor at the side of the body, mimicking the action of picking up a heavy suitcase. The offset loading creates a significant lateral anti-flexion demand on the core, requiring the obliques and quadratus lumborum to resist lateral bending throughout the lift. It develops functional carrying strength and core stability simultaneously.

execution.starting_position: Stand with a dumbbell or kettlebell on the floor to one side of the body. The weight is positioned beside the hip, not in front. Feet hip-width apart.
execution.setup_instructions: Begin with a moderate weight — the anti-lateral-flexion demand can be deceiving. Perform equal reps on both sides.
steps: Step 1: Stand with the weight to the right side of the body.
Step 2: Hinge at the hip and bend the knee to reach the weight with the right hand.
Step 3: Brace the core hard and resist the pull to lean toward the weight.
Step 4: Drive through the floor and stand tall, keeping the torso perfectly vertical.
Step 5: Lower under control to the floor. Complete all reps, then switch sides.
execution.breathing_instructions: Brace before each rep. Exhale at lockout.
common_mistakes: Leaning toward the loaded side — the torso must remain vertical throughout
Reaching too far to the side, compromising the hip hinge pattern
Using a weight so heavy that lateral flexion cannot be resisted
safety_considerations: If the torso cannot be kept vertical, reduce the load
Perform equal volume on both sides to prevent asymmetry development
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full hip extension at the top. Weight returns to the floor between reps.
coaching_cues: Stand tall — don't lean toward the weight
Carry it like you don't want anyone to notice
